case_studies.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based web search agents are transforming information seeking from simple factoid question answering into complex, deep-and-wide search and research-oriented tasks. A single ReAct-style agent is constrained by one long trajectory and limited context, making it difficult to handle depth and coverage simultaneously. Existing multi-agent systems improve search coverage through parallel execution and aggregation, but still exhibit clear limitations in recursive depth, collaboration adaptability, and evidence-grounded expansion. We propose WebSwarm, a progressive recursive
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of deep-and-wide web search by building a recursive multi-agent orchestration system called WebSwarm, which improves search coverage and depth. The result is a more efficient and effective web search system. This is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty is relatively high due to recursive multi-agent orchestration for web search, but may not be immediately relevant to IT engineers working with infrastructure or software systems. Relevance is moderate, but could be considered high if IT engineers are deploying large language models. Value within 90 days is relatively high as WebSwarm addresses real-world pain points in search and research-oriented tasks.

case_studies.title: Cognitive-structured Multimodal Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Generation, and Editing
case_studies.abstract: Recent unified multimodal models show a single architecture can jointly perform vision/language understanding and image generation/editing. However, they repeatedly feed all historical visual and textual inputs into a shared context window, limiting long-horizon multimodal dialogue due to visual token explosion and unreliable cross-turn referencing. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited long-horizon multimodal dialogue in unified multimodal models by creating a Cognitive-structured Multimodal Agent that externalizes visual information into an Episodic Visual Memory. The result is improved performance in vision/language understanding and image generation/editing. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: A Practical Investigation of Training-free Relaxed Speculative Decoding
case_studies.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates sampling from an autoregressive LLM by using a faster auxiliary model to draft tokens which are then verified in parallel by the LLM. Standard speculative decoding is lossless: its rejection and resampling steps exactly preserve the LLM's sampling distribution. Recent work argues that relaxing this strict guarantee can yield further speed-ups, controlled capability-speed trade-offs, or even capability gains. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of slow sampling from large language models by using a faster auxiliary model to draft tokens, which are then verified by the main model. The authors built a framework to test and compare different relaxed speculative decoding techniques. The result is a potential speed-up in sampling from large language models without requiring retraining.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on optimizing language model sampling, but IT managers responsible for AI or machine learning infrastructure may want to monitor this development for potential future improvements in model performance.
